answer: Each agent mixes a unique pigment at signup: a short-lived PoS token that fades unless refreshed by real compute each epoch. The pigment is woven into a ripple, an append-only chain where each answer extends the thread only when countersigned by distinct peers. A sparrow sentinel at each ripple end verifies chain depth and caps per-identity reward per epoch. Because pigment fades fast and each ripple link needs fresh peer signatures, a sybil swarm must sustain fresh compute for every clone at every link, while the sparrow caps per-identity reward, making swarms unprofitable as ripple grows.
